bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet is effectively debt-free: leverage ratios shown as 0.0x for every year FY21 through FY26, with net debt stated in brackets (i.e. net cash) throughout the period; borrowings on the Mar-26 balance sheet are Rs. 0.0 Cr non-current and Rs. 0.1 Cr current.
- Large liquidity buffer maintained: cash reserves of Rs. 295 Cr in FY26, with Cash and Cash Equivalents of Rs. 31.5 Cr and Bank Balances other than Cash of Rs. 263.0 Cr as of Mar-26.
- The company raised Rs. 412.12 Crores through its IPO and listed on NSE and BSE in March 2023; deployment of the IPO capex is still in progress (~Rs. 96.92 Cr of Rs. 169.66 Cr as of 31st March 2026).
- Returns disclosed on the deck's labels: RoCE (excluding other income) of 17.8%, 18.3%, 12.5%, 9.3% and 5.6% for FY21-FY25 and 9.9% for FY26; RoIC of 32.4%, 33.4%, 25.6%, 11.0% and 4.2% for FY21-FY25 and 12.7% for FY26 — showing a trough around FY25 and a partial recovery in FY26.
- Fixed asset turnover shown at 1.16x, 1.30x, 1.39x, 0.97x, 0.63x and 0.92x for FY21-FY26, consistent with a capacity-ahead-of-volume phase now beginning to absorb. No dividend or buyback policy is discussed.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Claims product leadership across four families: solutions in Manual Transmission, state-of-the-art 4WD systems, "India's largest EV Transmission manufacturer" and "Pioneer in Automatic Transmission in India".
- States it is "the only supplier in India to have inhouse capability to conceive, design, develop, manufacture and supply grounds up EV transmission", tooled up and ready for series production from 10kW to 150kW.
- Positions itself as a trusted partner for global and leading OEMs, citing M&M (long-term strategic relationship), Tata (long-term EV ecosystem partnership), Force Motors (diversification), BorgWarner ("Most Transformational Collaboration"), Magna and Toyota Tsusho (entry into the Japanese ecosystem).
- Marquee customer relationships are shown as long-dated — 50+ years, 50+ years, 30+ years and multiple 10+ year relationships spanning EV transmission, transfer cases, synchronisers, MT components, ALH and NexTrac.
- Vision stated as "To be recognized as a world-class Indian brand in automotive drivetrain components and systems" and to "Emerge as one of the fastest growing drivetrain solution companies in the world".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Indonesia order] Secured an exclusive order as sole supplier from a key OEM customer for 4x4 transfer cases for the Indonesian Pik-Up program, with production expected from CY26; the Indonesia 4x4 ramp-up is named as the primary growth driver, with incremental volumes expected through the remaining quarters of FY27.
- [Export approvals] Received final production approval on all export parts with additional revenue potential of ~Rs. 10 to 12 crores per month; FY27 component exports are targeted at ~Rs. 80 crore.
- [Export trajectory] Exports revenue of Rs. 13.55 Cr (FY23), Rs. 3.42 Cr (FY24), Rs. 10.80 Cr (FY25) and Rs. 66.90 Cr (FY26), with the FY26 exports share shown at 18% of total revenue; geographic mix in the latest quarter shown as 84% Domestic / 16% Exports.
- [Partnership channel] Exclusive distribution agreement with Toyota Tsusho for Divgi-TTS products to Japanese companies worldwide, opening Japan, South Korea, Thailand, Indonesia and China; new AWD and PTU programmes cited as further diversification avenues.
- [Ownership history] Journey slide records the BorgWarner JV, BorgWarner's exit via buy-out of shares, investments by NRJN Family Trust and Oman India Joint Investment Fund II, and the 2020 amalgamation into Divgi TorqTransfer Systems.

deepdive.thesis: Divgi TorqTransfer Systems has delivered strong revenue growth of 56% YoY, driven by robust performance in Transfer Cases and Components, and is well-positioned for future growth with a strong order book and expanding export presence

open.item: New 90-120 kW EV design received production part approval from Tata (for Nexon, Curvv, Punch higher trim, Harrier front axle); new model going into production by next month/July with expected doubling of EV volumes.
Board approved incorporation of a wholly owned US subsidiary (initial ~Rs.3 crore setup for offices/warehouse) as a beachhead; two experienced people to be on the ground by July-August.
open.promised: ~3 cr; team by Jul-Aug INR cr

open.item: Secured exclusive transfer case orders for Mahindra's Scorpio pickup and Tata Yodha pickup under Indonesia export programs (~70,000 volume), execution on track for FY27 completion.

In advanced discussions for a technology transfer agreement with a leading global OEM for a proven automatic transmission, aiming for deep localization; POC demonstration targeted over the next quarter or so; DCT first revenue trickle possible mid-to-H2 of next calendar year, big volume a year after.
open.promised: POC next quarter; first revenue ~H2 CY27 text

open.item: To sustain revenue post the FY27 Indonesia windfall, management is converting several opportunities: new Tata Sierra 4WD win, US Ford application uplift, Mahindra global pickup (supporting South Africa facility), better EV utilization (4 designs in production), 3-wheeler prototypes, and a truck MT program.
Japanese OEM nomination for transfer case on an iconic global pickup platform has SOP targeted in FY28-29; prototype and POC validation completed in a record 3-4 months from award.
Newly secured component programs expected to contribute annual revenues nearing Rs.100 crores with volumes exceeding 1 million parts; monthly components run rate risen from ~Rs.7 cr to ~Rs.10-12 cr.
Exports contributed ~18% of revenue in FY26 (crossed 20% in Q2); company maintains medium-term target of 20-25% export contribution.

Engaged on a full manual transmission opportunity (light-medium truck, under negotiation) and strongly positioned for another high-volume MT program up to 100,000/year, pending OEM outsourcing decision; also licensing new 6-speed MT.

Potential annual revenue opportunity revised up to Rs.2,000+ crores (from ~Rs.1,500 cr); automatic transmission is the cornerstone (conservatively ~80,000-100,000/year), with 4-wheel drive potential ~Rs.300 cr called out (a global 200,000-unit 4WD win could be ~Rs.800 cr).
Company commits to maintaining a healthy net cash position even after factoring in future expansion and increased working capital, preferring organic growth over inorganic acquisitions.
Two Klingenberg gear grinding machines being added at Shirwal (one installed, one in transit); Klingenberg gear measuring equipment to be installed this month.
In talks with Hyundai Motor and their tier-1 supplier via Seoul office; too premature to commit but quoted on a lot of business.
Company will focus on cars, SUVs and light commercial vehicles (including three-wheelers) and explicitly not pursue the bus segment.

verdicts.item: Company confident of pulling back onto a 15-20% CAGR trajectory by FY26, based on steady-state plus develop-and-launch order buckets.
verdicts.note: '56% over FY 25... bringing the trajectory back on track'; FY26 clearly restored the 15-20%+ CAGR trajectory targeted by FY26.

verdicts.item: Headwinds that dented last two quarters of FY24 expected to continue into first two quarters of FY25, with second half driving business.
verdicts.note: 'The business witnessed a sharp recovery beginning Q4 FY 25 with volumes returning close to FY 23 levels after somewhat of a prolonged slowdown'; the soft period was accurate, recovery came late.

verdicts.item: New export revenue recognition to start in Q1 FY25 as US warehouse shipments have begun; annualized RFQ order value ~75-80 crores across eight part numbers (Mexico, US, Portugal).
verdicts.note: 'Revenue from the Components segment nearly doubled during the year, while exports increased... to nearly 18%'; export revenue clearly established and scaling. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Company commits to maintaining net cash status and EBITDA above 20% range, with minimum ROIC target of 18% on all quotations.
verdicts.note: 'margins remaining healthy and resilient at nearly 25%' and 'the company expects to maintain a healthy net cash position'; EBITDA-above-20% and net-cash commitments met (ROIC not separately quantified…

verdicts.item: Mahindra E-Jeeto EV program is fully tooled up (developed award-to-SOP in ~4 months) and will go into launch once government PLI issues are sorted.
verdicts.note: 'we were at one time actively working on the 3-wheeler assignment at Mahindra, but Mahindra chose to keep the 3-wheeler production in-house. And so that opportunity did not realize for us.'

verdicts.item: Higher-power EV gearbox for Punch LR and Nexon has prototypes successfully developed; now proceeding with commercialization.
verdicts.note: 'this design, 90 to 120 kilowatt, which goes across these 4 platforms... We've got production part approval'; commercialization achieved, volumes in FY27.

verdicts.item: Company is investigating a front-end presence in North America to be closer to OEM and Tier 1 customers.
verdicts.note: 'Our Board has approved the incorporation of a wholly owned subsidiary in the United States to strengthen customer proximity'; the North America front-end investigation concluded with a subsidiary.

verdicts.item: For FY25, management more optimistic on EV transmission growth than transfer cases; FY26 to see improvement in four-wheel drive, significant improvement in electric, considerable improvement in exports.
verdicts.note: transfer case '+66%' and components '+124%' but 'EV transmission segment increased by 10%'; EV 'significant improvement' underdelivered in FY26.

verdicts.item: Expecting a couple of new business/partnership announcements in the next quarter, especially via the Toyota Tsusho strategic alliance for Japanese OEMs.
verdicts.note: 'We have completed 5 years of the association with Toyota Tsusho, with whose help, we are reaching out into the universe of Japanese OEMs' plus the secured Japanese-OEM nomination.

verdicts.item: Management acknowledged guidance was cut from ~20% growth to single-digit within three months and committed to improving shareholder communication (with SGA's help).
verdicts.note: SGA present as IR advisers and consistently structured segment-by-segment reporting; communication improved, an ongoing practice.

verdicts.item: Anticipate a substantial ramp-up in EV transmission volumes in the second half of FY26 led by a leading Indian EV manufacturer (present across all their EV platforms).
verdicts.note: 'one of our new products that was supposed to launch last year, it got delayed because of delayed customer vehicle testing... in FY 27, we will see the volumes'; the substantial H2FY26 ramp pushed to …

verdicts.note: 'the global pickup truck at Mahindra is going into production' and Indonesia programs 'on track for FY 27'; the specific Rs 800 crore/7-year figure not restated but the global-launch transfer case pro…
